claim: The Agricultural Revolution beginning around 10000 BCE enabled permanent settlements and the rise of complex societies
Writing was independently invented in Mesopotamia Egypt China and Mesoamerica between 3400 and 600 BCE
The Roman Empire at its height controlled the entire Mediterranean basin and extended from Britain to Mesopotamia
The Black Death killed approximately one-third of Europe's population between 1347 and 1353
The Scientific Revolution of the 16th and 17th centuries established empirical observation and mathematical reasoning as the basis for knowledge
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century transforming manufacturing from hand production to machine-based processes
The abolition of slavery was achieved through a combination of slave resistance economic changes and moral campaigning across the 18th and 19th centuries
The French Revolution of 1789 established the principles of liberty equality and fraternity that influenced democratic movements worldwide
World War II resulted in approximately 70 to 85 million deaths making it the deadliest conflict in human history
The Green Revolution of the 1960s and 1970s dramatically increased agricultural yields through high-yield crop varieties fertilizers and irrigation
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 symbolized the end of the Cold War and the reunification of Europe
The Columbian Exchange transferred crops animals diseases and ideas between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia after 1492
The Enlightenment promoted reason individual rights and skepticism of authority as foundations of modern democratic societies
The Silk Road connected East Asia to the Mediterranean for over 1500 years facilitating trade in goods ideas and technologies
The invention of the telegraph in the 1830s was the first technology to enable near-instantaneous long-distance communication
The Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 established the modern concept of state sovereignty and non-interference in internal affairs
The Harappan civilization of the Indus Valley developed urban planning with standardized weights drainage systems and grid streets by 2600 BCE
Paper was invented in China around 105 CE and reached Europe via the Islamic world by the 12th century
The decolonization movement after World War II led to the independence of over 80 nations across Asia and Africa
The invention of the compass in China during the Han dynasty revolutionized navigation and enabled transoceanic exploration
